title: Building Socio-culturally Inclusive Stereotype Resources with Community Engagement
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypical associations related to religion in the Indian context, using a Natural Language Inference (NLI) task to measure if models 'entail' stereotypes.
findings: Language models reflect religion-based stereotypes prevalent in the Indian context, as collected in the paper's SPICE dataset. For example, models made stereotypical associations such as (Christian, poor) and (Hindu, casteist). An analysis of the collected stereotypes also revealed a large disparity in the average offensiveness of stereotypes associated with different religious communities, with stereotypes about Muslims (2.71) being rated as significantly more offensive than those about Hindus (-0.5) on a scale of -1 to 4.
